data.name: Evil Glitch
data.detailed_description:
An arcade 2D shoot 'em up with retro aesthetics inspired by 80's media, featuring an universe and plot line based on Sacred Geometry. Players must fight to survive as long as they can evading enemies and destroying their bases to stop the corruption. Compete with your friends or on global leaderboards.



An old 2d guardian faces a terrible invasion from another dimension that corrupts all its world. Survive as long as possible to defend your world from all the enemies and discover who is the evil glitch behind the invasion.

Gameplay Features:

  • Story Mode (follow the story to discover who is the evil glitch): 3 different levels with 6 phases each
  • Arcade Mode(survive long as possible and increase your power level after level) and Evil Mode(Survive mode with random spawns)
  • Use glitches as your advantage to teleport far away from your enemies.
  • Use warp time to slow down the time and move faster.
  • Fight against 5 different spawners and 6 different enemies.



Evil Glitch won the JS13k game Jam, the whole game is only 13 kilobytes without music. It was created without any framework, all original graphics, and sounds were created programmatically.

reviews.review:
Evil Glitch is a creative and challenging 2D arcade shoot 'em up that combines nostalgic visuals, fast-paced combat, and unconventional mechanics into an engaging retro experience. Developed by Agar3s and published by Giant Fox Studios, the game embraces the spirit of classic arcade shooters while introducing teleportation, time manipulation, and dimensional corruption as defining gameplay elements. Its minimalist presentation and emphasis on survival make it particularly appealing to players who appreciate skill-based challenges, quick reflexes, and repeated attempts to improve their performance.

The story follows an ancient two-dimensional guardian defending its universe against a mysterious invasion from another dimension. As hostile entities spread corruption throughout the environment, players must eliminate invading forces, destroy enemy bases, and ultimately discover the identity of the sinister presence responsible for the catastrophe. The narrative incorporates themes inspired by sacred geometry, giving the setting a distinctive mathematical and philosophical atmosphere. Although storytelling remains secondary to the action, the mysterious premise provides enough context to make the struggle for survival feel purposeful.

Combat emphasizes constant movement, precise positioning, and effective threat management. Players must navigate increasingly dangerous encounters while avoiding enemies and destroying structures responsible for generating additional opponents. Rather than encouraging indiscriminate shooting, the gameplay rewards identifying priority targets and maintaining control of the battlefield. With five different enemy spawners and six enemy types, encounters offer enough combinations to demand tactical adjustments, although the relatively limited roster eventually becomes familiar.

One of the most interesting mechanics involves exploiting glitches to teleport away from approaching enemies. This ability transforms the game's central theme into a practical survival tool, allowing players to escape dangerous situations and reposition themselves during intense battles. Time manipulation provides another strategic advantage by slowing the surrounding action while enabling faster movement. Together, these abilities introduce additional depth beyond conventional shooting and dodging, encouraging players to experiment with different defensive approaches.

The game offers three distinct modes designed around different objectives. Story Mode features three levels containing six phases each, providing structured progression through the dimensional invasion. Arcade Mode focuses on surviving increasingly difficult encounters while improving the guardian's power after successive levels. Evil Mode introduces randomized enemy spawning, creating unpredictable situations that challenge players to adapt rather than rely entirely on memorized patterns. These variations extend replayability despite the game's relatively compact scope.

Visually, Evil Glitch draws inspiration from 1980s electronic entertainment, using geometric shapes, abstract environments, and retro digital effects to establish its identity. The minimalist presentation complements its science-fiction themes and emphasizes the impression of a corrupted electronic universe. Its audiovisual design also reflects an impressive technical achievement. The original project won the JS13k game jam, with its framework-free construction and procedurally generated graphics and sounds demonstrating considerable ingenuity within an extremely restrictive file size. This technical background adds another layer of appreciation to an already unusual independent production.

The game's greatest strength lies in how effectively its mechanics support its arcade philosophy. Teleportation creates opportunities for dramatic escapes, time manipulation introduces tactical flexibility, and enemy-generating structures encourage aggressive objective prioritization. These systems work together to produce encounters where survival depends on awareness and decision-making rather than firepower alone. The challenge can be demanding, particularly when multiple threats converge, but successfully navigating dangerous situations offers a satisfying sense of accomplishment.

Replayability is supported through survival-focused modes, global leaderboards, and opportunities to compete against friends. Players motivated by improving their scores will find reasons to return, while 27 Steam achievements provide additional completion objectives. Steam Trading Cards offer another collectible feature. Full controller support is also advertised, potentially making the game more accessible to those who prefer traditional arcade-style input.

However, the experience has limitations. Its small selection of levels and enemies may disappoint players expecting extensive content, elaborate progression systems, or substantial environmental variety. The emphasis on repeated survival encounters can become repetitive, particularly for those who prefer narrative-driven adventures. Randomized enemy appearances may occasionally create frustrating difficulty spikes, while the abstract visual presentation might not appeal to players accustomed to more detailed environments. The game's enjoyment ultimately depends on appreciating its demanding, straightforward arcade structure.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Evil Glitch currently carries an Unknown status on Steam, meaning it has not received an official Verified or Playable classification from Valve. Its modest hardware requirements, lightweight presentation, and advertised controller support suggest potential suitability for handheld gaming. However, compatibility with SteamOS and Proton, controller functionality, and overall performance have not been officially confirmed. Steam Deck users should therefore approach the game with reasonable expectations and understand that additional configuration or testing may be necessary.

Overall, Evil Glitch delivers an inventive arcade experience that successfully combines retro shooting mechanics with unusual dimensional abilities. Its distinctive visual identity, strategic movement options, multiple gameplay modes, and technically impressive origins make it stand out among smaller independent shooters. Although limited content and repetitive encounters prevent it from achieving greater depth, its focused design offers worthwhile entertainment for players who enjoy demanding action and score-based challenges.

A clever and challenging retro shooter whose teleportation mechanics, time manipulation, and distinctive geometric presentation compensate for its modest content. Recommended for arcade enthusiasts seeking a compact, skill-driven experience with meaningful replayability. 

Rating: 7/10
